title: The first hot air balloon flight
claimSupported: The Montgolfier brothers demonstrate balloon flight at Versailles. A sheep, a duck, and a rooster rode in a balloon before people did!

title: Iconic objects: the voltaic pile
claimSupported: Volta introduces his electric battery, called the voltaic pile. The first electric battery was called a “pile.”

title: Trevithick’s model road locomotive engine
claimSupported: Trevithick builds early steam railway locomotives. One of Trevithick’s locomotives was named “Catch Me Who Can.”

title: Who is credited with inventing the telephone?
claimSupported: Bell receives his telephone patent and demonstrates working speech transmission. Bell’s famous early telephone message asked his assistant to come to him.

title: The origins of sound recording
claimSupported: Edison develops a phonograph that records and plays back sound. Recording sound and playing it back were once two different challenges!

title: Timeline of Edison and his inventions
claimSupported: Edison’s team makes an incandescent bulb that shines for over 13 hours. Edison’s team tried hundreds of experiments while working on their light bulb.

title: Benz Patent Motor Car: 1885–1886
claimSupported: Benz develops his practical gasoline car and files its patent. Benz’s first gasoline car had three wheels!

title: Josephine Garis Cochran
claimSupported: Cochran receives a patent for her practical dishwashing machine. Cochran designed separate wire spaces to hold plates, cups, and saucers.

title: Willis Haviland Carrier
claimSupported: Carrier’s modern system controls temperature and humidity in a printing plant. Carrier’s first air-conditioning installation helped a printing factory.

title: First flights: December 17, 1903
claimSupported: The Wright brothers make controlled, powered flights at Kitty Hawk. The Wright brothers made four flights on their big day.

title: Slinky
publisher: The Strong National Museum of Play
claimSupported: Richard James discovers the spring motion that leads to the Slinky toy. The Slinky began with springs meant to keep equipment steady on ships.

title: Percy L. Spencer
claimSupported: Percy Spencer creates a device that cooks food with microwaves. The first microwave oven was given the name “Radarange.”

title: George de Mestral
claimSupported: George de Mestral patents his hook-and-loop fastener. Clingy plant burrs inspired the tiny hooks in Velcro.

title: Sputnik: the dawn of the space age
claimSupported: Sputnik becomes the first artificial satellite to orbit Earth. The first space satellite was about the size of a beach ball.

title: The stud and tube principle
claimSupported: LEGO files the patent for its stud-and-tube brick connection. The tubes underneath a LEGO brick help it grip other bricks.

title: Firsts: the mouse
claimSupported: Engelbart’s team develops its first computer mouse prototype. The first computer mouse had a wooden shell and just one button.

title: Evolution of the Rubik’s Cube
publisher: The Strong National Museum of Play
claimSupported: Ernő Rubik creates his twisting cube puzzle. The Rubik’s Cube was first called the “Magic Cube.”

title: Steven Sasson
claimSupported: Steven Sasson builds a self-contained digital camera at Kodak. Sasson’s digital camera used 16 batteries!

title: Our timeline of innovation
claimSupported: The burr-inspired idea dates to 1941, followed by a decade of development and patent milestones in the 1950s.

title: Steam train in Kensington Gardens
claimSupported: Trevithick built a steam railway locomotive in 1804.
